description: 🪨 why use many token when few token do trick. Viral skill + proxy for coding agents that cuts 65% of tokens by talking like a caveman.
vibe: Why use many token when few token do trick — but route every repo like a paranoid monorepo architect.
highlights: Binding cross-repo routing table: each concern (skills, Engine, MV3 extension, Agent SDK, Browse driver, Pebble) has exactly one owning repository.
Explicit visibility policy per repo — public, private-during-development, or private commercial — declared up front to prevent accidental leaks.
Skills are pulled in via @-imports rather than duplicated, keeping the instruction file a thin router instead of a monolith.
Hard rule to read CLAUDE.md before any repository work, establishing a single source of truth for agent behavior.
Absolute filesystem paths for sibling repos, removing ambiguity about where work belongs.
assessment: This file treats agent instructions as a routing layer rather than a knowledge dump, which is unusually disciplined for a viral-toy repo. By pinning each workstream to a specific repo and visibility tier, it prevents the classic failure mode of agents editing the wrong codebase or leaking private commercial source into public PRs. The @-import pattern keeps the file short while still composing rich skill definitions, matching the project's own 'few token do trick' ethos.
